title: Arrow vs function

blocks.md:
## Shorter is not the whole story

`const add = (a, b) => a + b` is shorter. An arrow also **does not get its own `this`**. It keeps the `this` from the scope where it was created.

A method that needs `this.dir` should stay a `function`, or you bind it later. This lesson is syntax plus that preview — no page tree yet.

If the fox writes an arrow as `go` on a route object, `this.dir` is not the route. A plain `function go()` would see the object that called it.

choices.md: Whatever called it, like a method
The `this` from the scope where it was created

blocks.explainMd: Arrows do not get a new this at the call site. They keep the this from where they were written.
